about: Seconds per mutation row. secondsPerRow is measured on the CI runner from the shard logs of two full runs of every harness: each harness's measured seconds over its rows, averaged. secondsPerRowLabel, for each harness CI runs in slices, is inferred, not measured: no run records a row's own time, so each slice's measured seconds are shared among its rows in proportion to one plus the tests each turned red, averaged over the runs. secondsPerIntegrationRow is the mean of those inferred costs over a harness's integration rows, the rate for an integration row with no cost of its own. The plan weights shards by these so no shard nears its time limit. A harness missing here is planned at defaultSecondsPerRow, and any other row missing from its harness's labels at that harness's rate; re-measure when a shard runs past fifteen minutes. Cost a new row from CI, never from a run on a developer machine, whose times are not the runner's. A new row that runs a suite other rows of its harness already run is costed at the mean of their costs by label. A row whose suite no row runs yet has no cost by label until a CI run has run it, its own pull request's run included, and is planned meanwhile at its harness's rate, or its integration rate for an integration row; its cost is then the measured seconds of the slice that ran it, less what this table gives the slice's other rows, shared among its new rows. Do not leave it at the rate once CI has run it: rows left there though their suites take four times it on CI planned a slice at nine minutes that CI ran for twenty-eight. The costs by label, rates and integration rate of mutate-workspace-boundary-guards.js and mutate-sdlc-gate-guards.js are derived from the shard logs of CI runs 42596195029, 42600452339, 42601132361, 42612674381, 42613267711, 42617502454, 42625901207, 42626462142, 42630320371, 42631470848, 42631520174, 42633231846 and 42640417868: every run on 2026-11-09 that ran the boundary harness, from the first to hold its "Folder reads:" rows to 42640417868, because a row runs its whole suite, so a suite that gains tests slows every row on it, and older runs time suites that have since grown. Their slices are shared by suite, not by tests turned red: each slice's measured seconds are shared among its rows in proportion to the cost of the suite each row runs, that cost being the mean of the shares its rows were given, repeated from equal shares until no slice's estimate moves by more than a tenth of a percent in a pass; each label's shares are averaged over the runs, the rate is their mean over the harness's rows, and the integration rate their mean over its integration rows. Shared by tests turned red, a row that turned a hundred fast tests red took minutes of a slice CI ran in seconds. mutate-stale-session-guards.js is measured on a developer machine, one row at a time, its costs by label measured rather than inferred, until shard logs record it, and so is the one labelled row of mutate-history-guards.js. The rates of mutate-run-detail-guards.js and mutate-routines-truth-guards.js, which CI runs whole, are re-derived from the same runs as each harness's measured seconds over its rows, averaged; a harness run whole gives no slices to tell its rows apart, so neither keeps costs by label. mutate-routines-guards.js has costs by label for some of its rows only, measured on a developer machine one row at a time; its other rows are planned at the harness rate. The state file rows labelled under mutate-atomic-write-guards.js and mutate-routines-guards.js are measured the same way, on a developer machine, one row at a time, and so are the workspace switch rows labelled under mutate-routines-guards.js. Those costs from a developer machine predate the rule above and stand until shard logs record their rows. The time-zone rows of mutate-routine-editor-guards.js and mutate-routines-guards.js are costed by the rule above: each at the mean cost by label of its harness's rows on the same suite, the two on doc-claims.test.js, which no other row of their harness runs, at the mean of the two boundary rows on that suite, whose costs come from CI, and the four on schedule-zone.test.js, which no other row runs, at their harness's rate, because CI runs both harnesses whole and so gives no slice that tells their rows apart. Three set-of-days rows, two under mutate-routines-guards.js and one under mutate-routine-editor-guards.js, are costed at the mean of the costs by label of the rows that run the same suite. The set-of-days rows that run test/unit/routine-days.test.js, a suite no other row runs, have no cost by label: CI has only run them inside a whole harness, whose measured seconds less what this table gives its other rows is that harness's drift against the table rather than what those rows take, so they are planned at their harness's rate until a CI shard log times them apart from the rest of their harness.
